page.layout: One block of verse in a single column, with the page number at the head. A catchword stands at the far right below the last line. No running head, no notes.

main_text.p: Seris & uberem parentum prorogat Hereditatem posteris. Quin intonat quando hinc & inde tristibus Fortuna laeua cladibus, Et res,& omne uita cuius indiget, His affluenter suppetent. Praui peribunt, ceu uorax uelociter Depascit ignis uictimam. Cum mutuatur impius, reddit nihil. At iustus usq; pauperum Miseritus, ipse utcunq; parce uictitet, Prodest, iuuatq;, & commodat. Hinc tanta tanq; larga praemia obtinet, Vt quisquis hunc dilexerit, Deoq; ametur: quisquis oderit, Deum Hostem grauemq; is sentiat. In calle ueri Dominus ipsum deniq; Deducit, & praeit uiam. Si forte greßus turbet error lubricus (Vt labimur caeci indies) Non reprobatur, sed uigore numinis Mox subleuatus ambulat. Puer fui,quodcunq; uixi & hactenus Acui, senex fi consulo, Iusti relicti exempla nulla conspicor, Prolis nec eius turpiter Egentis. hic ut mutuo det,eroget, Multa in fideles pauperes:

page.notes: The first line of the page reads "Seris" at the head of the verse; the text begins mid-poem, so it is a continuation. The line "Multa in fideles pauperes:" is underlined by a printed rule or ornament, which is not transcribed. The catchword "Bius" sits at the right margin beside the last line. Printed spelling kept: "greßus", "fi", "ametur", "Egentis". The lines are set as one stanza because no stanza break is visible.
